title: Denver Nuggets vs. Oklahoma City Thunder Live Score & Stats – October 22, 2026 Update on CBS Sports
body:
Denver’s home court turned into a proving ground for Oklahoma City on Tuesday night as the Thunder eked out a 112‑107 victory, snapping the Nuggets’ three‑game winning streak and sending a clear signal that the Western Conference’s early‑season hierarchy is far from settled. Jalen Williams led the charge for the Thunder with 21 points, while rookie big man Chet Holmgren dominated the glass with 17 rebounds and added 12 points, compensating for a surprisingly cold night from Shai‑Gilgeous‑Alexander, who managed just eight points on 2‑of‑12 shooting.

The Nuggets entered the matchup riding a 3‑0 start, anchored by Nikola Jokić’s 28‑point, 12‑assist performance and Jamal Murray’s 24 points off the bench. Yet Denver’s offensive rhythm faltered in the fourth quarter, as they shot a paltry 38 percent from the field and missed crucial free throws that allowed Oklahoma City to claw back from a double‑digit deficit. The loss marks Denver’s first stumble since the season opener and raises questions about their depth when the starting unit rests.

Oklahoma City’s win was built on a balanced attack that exploited Denver’s defensive lapses. After a sluggish first half, the Thunder surged in the third quarter, outscoring the Nuggets 34‑22. Williams’ ability to create off the dribble and finish at the rim proved decisive, while Holmgren’s presence in the paint forced Denver to double‑team, opening up perimeter opportunities for Josh Giddey, who contributed 15 points and six assists. Even with Shai‑Gilgeous‑Alexander’s off night, the Thunder’s collective scoring—four players in double figures—demonstrated a versatility that could trouble any opponent as the season progresses.

For Denver, the defeat underscores a lingering vulnerability in transition defense. The Nuggets allowed 19 fast‑break points, many generated by Holmgren’s long outlet passes and Williams’ quick cuts to the basket. Moreover, Denver’s reliance on Jokić as the primary playmaker left them exposed when he was forced into the post and unable to distribute effectively. Coach Michael Malone will likely reconsider his rotation, perhaps giving more minutes to forward Aaron Gordon, who showed flashes of defensive intensity but struggled to find offensive rhythm.

The game also highlighted the evolving dynamic between the two franchises. The Thunder, still in the early stages of a rebuild centered around Holmgren and Giddey, have shown that they can compete with established playoff contenders when they execute as a unit. Conversely, the Nuggets, despite their star power, must address consistency issues that could hinder their quest for a deep postseason run. Their next matchup against the Phoenix Suns will be a litmus test for whether they can rebound from this setback and reassert their dominance in the West.

Looking ahead, both teams have plenty to prove. Oklahoma City aims to solidify its identity and climb the standings, hoping that Holmgren’s rebounding prowess and Williams’ scoring can become a regular formula. Denver, on the other hand, must tighten its defensive communication and find alternative scoring avenues beyond Jokić and Murray. If the Nuggets can adjust quickly, they remain a formidable contender; if not, the early season turbulence could open the door for a surprise challenger in the race for the conference title.
